subject: POC Trial: Model selection & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Gomez <sofia@finbot.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC Trial: Model selection & success criteria

Hi Sofia / Carlos —

Thanks again for the chat today — great overview of FinBot's agent flows and the high-level metrics you care about. To recap from our discovery and propose next steps for a 3-week POC/trial:

Summary of needs (from today's call):
- Use-case: customer support summarization + suggested reply generation for English and Spanish
- Throughput: a mix of interactive queries (median QPS ~ 1-2) and batch re-runs (~200/day)
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 350ms per response for interactive flows
- Cost sensitivity: aiming to keep per-response inference cost as low as possible while maintaining quality
- Safety/robustness: handle noisy transcripts and code-switching between Spanish/English

Proposed POC timeline & scope:
1) Week 0 (this week): align on success criteria, test prompts, and dataset access; kickoff call
2) Week 1: baseline model runs + integration of Redwood SDK; initial eval on sample prompts
3) Week 2: tuning (prompt templates / temp control), batching & caching config, run extended evals
4) Week 3: side-by-side comparison, performance tuning, final review and decision

Suggested success criteria (please confirm):
- Qualitative: >= 85% accept rate from your CS team on suggested replies (sample of 200)
- Accuracy/Quality: top-1 relevance >= 88% on labeled test set
- Latency: P95 interactive < 350ms for selected config
- Cost: average token cost per response < $0.003 (target)

Model selection (initial recommendation):
- Primary: Mistral-Instruct / Mistral-7B-v0 (good instruction-following and cost profile)
- Fallback: Llama-2-13B-chat quantized (for noisy inputs and robust multi-turn memory)
- Multilingual: run a small Spanish validation subset; if quality drops significantly, we can trial a larger model (e.g., Llama-2-70B) for the Spanish flows only

Owners & next steps:
- FinBot (Sofia/Carlos): confirm success criteria, share a small sample of labeled prompts (200) and a handful of transcripts for Spanish code-switching cases
- Redwood (Marissa): finalize POC plan and send kickoff invite; coordinate AWS creds if needed for private trial data access
- Redwood (Aditya): propose exact model configs (quantization level, batch sizes) and provide test harness; set up initial eval scripts

I attached a draft POC plan and a sample CSV of test prompts to get started. Can you confirm the criteria and availability for a 30-minute kickoff early next week (Mon/Tue)?

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: FinBot-POC-Plan-v1.pdf (summary plan)
Attachment: POC-test-prompts.csv

From: Sofia Gomez <sofia@finbot.ai>

Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: POC Trial: Model selection & success criteria

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the POC outline. We're aligned on the overall timeline; a couple of clarifications from our side:

1) Multilingual requirement: Spanish is critical for ~30% of our traffic. We need to ensure the model preserves tone and can handle code-switched messages (EN/ES).
2) Evaluation metrics: in addition to the accept rate and relevance, we need to capture "hallucination" incidents (incorrect facts), and a small safety checklist for PII leakage on transcripts.
3) Latency: if possible, aim for P95 < 300ms for English; we understand Spanish may be higher for larger models.

We're preparing the 200 labeled prompts and ~50 messy transcripts for the code-switching cases. We'll upload them to the Drive link you shared by EOD Monday.

Model question: we think cost will be a big factor. Curious about your recommendation for primary vs fallback. We prefer starting with a smaller, cheaper model if it meets quality for English, and only escalate to larger models for Spanish if needed.

Kickoff: Mon 23 Feb at 10am PT works for our team.

Thanks —
Sofia
Head of Product | FinBot
sofia@finbot.ai | +1 (415) 555-7788

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC Trial: Model selection & success criteria

Hi Sofia —

Quick note from the SE side on model choices and evaluation approach. High-level recommendations based on your constraints (cost-sensitivity, Spanish coverage, robustness to noisy transcripts):

Primary model (cost-first baseline):
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (quantized to int8/4 if possible)
  - Why: strong instruction-following, favorable cost/latency on modern GPUs, good for English conversational summarization.
  - Expected perf: typically low latency (P95 < 250ms on a single A100 80GB/gpu with continuous batching) for short prompts.

Fallback / robust option for noisy + multilingual:
- Llama-2-13B-chat (int8 quant) or Falcon-40B-instruct if we need more robustness
  - Why: larger-context handling and better multilingual coverage; tradeoff is higher cost and latency.

Spanish strategy:
- Start with Mistral-7B-Instruct on Spanish subset; if automatic metrics (BLEU/ROUGE + human accept rate) fall >10 points behind English baseline, run a targeted trial of Llama-2-13B-chat for Spanish flows only.

Evaluation plan & ownership:
- Redwood/Aditya: provide evaluation harness and Dockerized runner, plus an initial script for measuring latency, token cost, and basic hallucination flags (heuristic checks)
- FinBot/Sofia: provide labeled prompts and the 50 transcripts (including code-switched) and a small human-review panel (4 reviewers) for accept-rate labeling
- Success gating: combination of automated metrics (relevance, hallucination count, latency/cost) and human accept-rate >= 85%

Technical notes:
- Quantization: we'll aim for int8 for Mistral; we'll document the exact quantization artifacts and a fallback to int16 if hallucinations appear to spike
- Caching & batching: we'll test prefix caching for repeated context (threaded conversations) and continuous batching to hit cost targets

I'll drop the initial runner and prompt harness into the Drive link tonight. Marissa — we'll need access to any internal test buckets / AWS role if you want us to run against your infra.

-Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

1) FinBot (Sofia/Carlos): upload labeled prompts + transcripts to Drive by EOD Monday (we have the upload link).
